title: The Amazon Treaty: What It Is For

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *para que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 4: it says the purpose of an action when the second clause has a new subject (*Te llamo para que vengas*). With the same subject you use *para* + infinitive. Treaties and summits exist for a purpose, so this pattern is at home here. Here it works on the Amazon Cooperation Treaty.

sections.title: Purpose with para que
rows: Los países crearon una secretaría para que la cooperación fuera permanente.
*para que* + imperfect subjunctive after a past verb
Los pueblos indígenas participan en los diálogos para que sus propuestas lleguen a los gobiernos.
*para que* + present subjunctive: a new subject
Los gobiernos firmaron el tratado para proteger la cuenca.
Se reúnen cada cierto tiempo para que los acuerdos se cumplan.

items.spanish: Los ocho países firmaron el tratado para que la región tuviera una política común.
items.english: The eight countries signed the treaty so that the region would have a common policy.

items.spanish: Los científicos miden la deforestación para que los gobiernos conozcan los datos.
items.english: Scientists measure deforestation so that governments know the figures.

items.spanish: Los países se reúnen para decidir acciones conjuntas.
items.english: The countries meet to decide joint actions.

sections.content: After *para que* the verb is always subjunctive: present for a present or future purpose, imperfect after a past verb. If the same person does both actions, use *para* + infinitive, never *para que*.
